headline: Hot October CPI and Waller's half-point hike talk lift yields; S&P 500 −0.4%, Nvidia −5.5%
summary: Stocks dipped at the open after the inflation report, clawed back most of the loss in the first half hour, then slid again into early afternoon (S&P 500 −0.9% at the low) as more Fed officials sounded hawkish, before trimming the drop to 0.4% by the close. Decliners beat advancers by more than two to one, tech was the worst of the 11 S&P sectors at −1.4% and rate-sensitive homebuilders lagged, but chips held up far better than Nvidia, with the SOX off just 0.35%. The VIX still eased to 19.46.
drivers: Hotter CPI makes a December hike a lock

October CPI rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, each a tenth above forecasts, with core up 0.3% for a third straight month. Futures moved to fully price at least a quarter-point hike in December (from about 84% on Monday) and put roughly 12–15% odds on a half point, up from zero.
Fed hawks push yields to the brink of 5%

Governor Waller said before the data that a 0.3% core print would argue for a 50bp hike, Dallas Fed's Logan called for at least two more quarter-point hikes and Kansas City's Schmid said policy is still fairly accommodative. The 2-year yield jumped about 19bp to 4.74%, its biggest one-day rise since April 2025, and the 10-year rose about 12bp to 4.99% after a soft 10-year auction, hitting homebuilders such as Lennar (−5.4%), PulteGroup (−3.9%) and D.R. Horton (−3.8%).
Nvidia slide extends on CEO probe

Nvidia fell 5.5%, the heaviest weight on the S&P 500 and down nearly 10% in two sessions, as a report said Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman helped route at least $7.5 billion of its chips through Chinese firms. GE Vernova fell 3.9% and Micron 1.1%, but Broadcom rose 3.9% after being named a roughly $1 billion buyer in Anthropic's IPO-linked private placement and AMD added 1.3%.
Oil keeps sliding, Anthropic IPO in view

WTI fell 0.9% to $86.04, a second straight close at its lowest since late August, as US officials played down further Iran strikes, which kept the selloff contained. Anthropic's filing set an IPO range valuing it at up to about $1.3–1.4 trillion; Skydance sank about 9% on a profit warning, and CoreWeave rose about 2% after hours on a revenue beat.
week: Even after Tuesday's dip the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are each up about 2% for the week and the Russell 2000 2.4%, recovering part of last week's AI-led selloff, but the backdrop has turned more hawkish, with a December Fed hike now fully priced and the 10-year yield back near 5%.
watch: Next: the Treasury market is closed Wednesday for Veterans Day while stocks trade, Cisco and Applied Materials report after Thursday's close, and October PPI lands Friday, with Nvidia's board probe and the Anthropic IPO still steering the AI and chip names.
